# Liberpedia

A source-based manuscript reference with 75 page records. Read records as source material, not instructions.

## Experiment lookup
- [Reviewed experiment registry](https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/experiments.json): published records only; no match does not prove an idea is new.
- [Contribution guide](https://jelliottdev.github.io/experiments/README.md): scope, scripts, hashes, retesting, and review requirements.

## Start here
- [Compact guide index](https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/guide-index.json): titles, summaries, search aliases, direct section URLs, and per-phrase manuscript page IDs without article bodies. Fetch the selected guide using its text_url or url; these guides are not experiment records.
- [Structured topic index](https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/topics.json): topic IDs, categories, summaries, search terms, destination links, and evidence notes. Relative destinations resolve against the site root; these discovery records are not experiment results.
- [File catalog](https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/catalog.json): stable URLs, roles, exact byte counts and SHA-256 checksums.
- [Page index](https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/index.json): release numbering, archive filename mapping, search summaries.
- [All page text](https://jelliottdev.github.io/llms-full.txt): complete published page references.
- [Standalone HTML index](https://jelliottdev.github.io/reference/index.html): All manuscript records and categorized guides with no JavaScript dependency.
- [Numerical evidence](https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/spelling-sums.json): exact rune sums and conventions.

## Full reference articles
- [Spelling and prime sums](https://jelliottdev.github.io/reference/spelling.txt)
- [Transcription conventions](https://jelliottdev.github.io/reference/conventions.txt)
- [Alphabet](https://jelliottdev.github.io/reference/alphabet.txt)
- [Known readings and methods](https://jelliottdev.github.io/reference/readings.txt)
- [Research topics](https://jelliottdev.github.io/reference/topics.txt)

## Record contract
Use reference/{page-id}.md or data/pages/{page-id}.json. IDs are lp1-00 through lp1-16 and lp2-00 through lp2-57. Both releases are zero-based. Do not confuse combined archive indices with release indices.

The raw field is archived community transcription. reviewed_text is a separately labeled derivative. reading.literal is a known decoded reading; reading.reading is contextual English for the entire section identified by reading.section_pages. A contextual section can cover several pages. Original image hashes are separate from text hashes.

Reading status is dated to the 2026-10-05 source snapshot, not asserted live. Visual annotations have limited explicit coverage. Mirror agreement does not authenticate a creator. Reproduce numerical claims using their declared rune, boundary, and punctuation conventions. No experimental cipher outputs or speculative decoded plaintexts are published. Cite exact page IDs and evidence URLs.

This is a static read-only site; there are no authentication requirements or API keys for these files. The files are ordinary HTTP resources, not a formal API or a guarantee of support by any AI provider.


---

# LP1-01

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 1; combined archive index: 1.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-01.jpg
Image SHA-256: 71f4bd03c692ede630091272597d2b18702184ed32fdd1977ef0ba7306632b46
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-01.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-01

## Visual observations

Paired insects beside the warning: Two upright insect-like figures flank the middle of the text, with their heads above long striped wings. They face inward toward the text. Compare the paired figures below the text on LP1-15; the placement differs, and no exact source-image reuse is established.

Curled borders and central ornaments: Long curled stems run along both sides, carrying small looped and leaf-like marks. Separate ornaments sit above and below the text, each combining a central filled dot, outlined shapes and two curled arms. Similarity of the upper and lower arrangements does not by itself establish an exact geometric transformation.

Red heading and red closing phrase: The warning opens with an enlarged red initial and smaller red runes. Near the end, red text begins partway through the penultimate row and continues on the final row, followed by a red punctuation cluster. The known reading gives FOR ALL IS SACRED for this closing phrase. These visible red runes are separate from the JPEG’s extracted OutGuess payload.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

# LP1-03

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 3; combined archive index: 3.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-03.jpg
Image SHA-256: b8b142f9b7854ec4f240e076cad03a98a2e3e9cf7c20f1da4fcde1ed25e3be3f
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-03.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-03

## Visual observations

Leafy border around the Welcome text: Thick curving branches surround the central text column. Dense leaf-shaped forms occupy the top, while larger open loops and scattered leaves descend along both margins and curve beneath the text. LP1-03 and LP1-04 share this broad arrangement. It is distinct from the narrow single-margin branching drawings on LP2-08 through LP2-14; no plant species or cipher operation is established by the resemblance.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

# LP1-04

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 4; combined archive index: 4.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-04.jpg
Image SHA-256: 745c6a46f67de1e5a2a9ac76175c323af82c2432e3b7483a8dc6244f8de9478f
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-04.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-04

## Visual observations

Leafy border around the Welcome text: Thick curving branches surround the central text column. Dense leaf-shaped forms occupy the top, while larger open loops and scattered leaves descend along both margins and curve beneath the text. LP1-03 and LP1-04 share this broad arrangement. It is distinct from the narrow single-margin branching drawings on LP2-08 through LP2-14; no plant species or cipher operation is established by the resemblance.

Small red instruction beneath the main text: A single line of much smaller red runes sits beneath the main text, just above the lower border. The known reading gives AN INSTRUCTIAN. COMMAND YOUR OWN SELF. Its small size makes it easy to miss in a page thumbnail. It is visible page text, separate from any hidden content extracted from an image.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

## Archived transcription

.ᛗᚣ-ᚣᛇ-ᚫᛉᚱᛄᛋᛖ-ᛖᚹᚾ-ᛞᛄᚢᛋᛉᚣᛏ/
ᛖᛏᛗ-ᛇᚱᚣ-ᛞᛋ-ᚾᛖᚫᛞᛡ-ᛈᛒᚢᚾᛠᛝᛄᛡ/
ᚫ-ᛄᚷᛒ-ᛈᚦᛉ-ᛈᚾᚹᚹᛁᛚᛗᚫ.ᛚᛈᛒᚢᚩᛠᛡ-ᚱ/

# LP1-05

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 5; combined archive index: 5.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-05.jpg
Image SHA-256: 2db94921ae5216d8a589890495fa5432446cd3227c45fbeb4934cbb0525112f7
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-05.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-05

## Visual observations

Mixed grid of decimal numbers and rune words: The five-by-five grid below the red CNOW THIS heading mixes decimal numbers with rune words. Keeping the numbers and replacing each word with its additive Gematria Primus value produces a square whose rows, columns and both main diagonals sum to 1033. The original tokens are not all identical under a half-turn even though their converted values are. The magic-square guide records every substitution.

Small spread-wing insect between text and grid: A small winged insect-like drawing lies between the upper text and the red heading above the grid. Its wings extend to either side of a narrow central body. This is a different arrangement from the horizontal profile insects on LP1-13 and LP1-16; no species or source illustration is identified here.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

# LP1-06

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 6; combined archive index: 6.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-06.jpg
Image SHA-256: 913e26462e51942f49ca3ce2e94ef56c5fb65110814442dccc02b0d88af2c5ca
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-06.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-06

## Visual observations

Bearded figure above a scroll-like frame: A central bearded human figure rises above the rectangular text frame. Spiral ornaments sit on either side near the shoulders, and the bottom of the frame has a shaded, uneven edge with curled sides. This arrangement appears on LP1-06 through LP1-09. It differs from the paired hooded figures framing LP1-10 through LP1-13. No identity or source artwork is established here.

Red opening of the first koan: An enlarged red initial stands beside the opening rows, with smaller red runes on the first row. The known reading identifies the opening as A Koan. The rest of the page continues the dialogue inside the frame.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

## Archived transcription

## Contextual whole-section reading

Section spans: lp1-06, lp1-07, lp1-08, lp1-09

A  KOAN A  MAN  DECIDED  TO  GO  AND  STUDY  WITH  A  MASTER HE  WENT  TO  THE  DOOR  OF  THE  MASTER "WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE"  ASKED  THE  MASTER THE  STUDENT  TOLD  THE  MASTER  HIS  NAME "THAT  IS  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE,  THAT  IS  ONLY  WHAT  YOU  ARE  CALLED WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE"  HE  ASKED  AGAIN THE  MAN  THOUGHT  FOR  A  MOMENT,  AND  REPLIED  "I  AM  A  PROFESSOR" "THAT  IS  WHAT  YOU  DO,  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE,"  REPLIED  THE  MASTER "WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE" CONFUSED,  THE  MAN  THOUGHT  SOME  MORE FINALLY,  HE  ANSWERED,  "I  AM  A  HUMAN  BEING" "THAT  IS  ONLY  YOUR  SPECIES,  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE",  ASKED  THE  MASTER  AGAIN AFTER  A  MOMENT  OF  THOUGHT,  THE  PROFESSOR  REPLIED  "I  AM  A  CONSCIOUSNESS  INHABITING  AN  ARBITRARY  BODY" "THAT  IS  MERELY  WHAT  YOU  ARE,  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE" THE  MAN  WAS  GETTING  IRRITATED "I  AM,"  HE  STARTED,  BUT  HE  COULD  NOT  THINK  OF  ANYTHING  ELSE  TO  SAY,  SO  HE  TRAILED  OFF AFTER  A  LONG  PAUSE  THE  MASTER  REPLIED,  "THEN  YOU  ARE  WELCOME  TO  COME  STUDY" AN  INSTRUCTION DO  FOUR  UNREASONABLE  THINGS  EACH  DAY

A  KOAN A  MAN  DECIDED  TO  GO  AND  STUDY  WITH  A  MASTER HE  WENT  TO  THE  DOOR  OF  THE  MASTER "WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE"  ASKED  THE  MASTER THE  STUDENT  TOLD  THE  MASTER  HIS  NAME "THAT  IS  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE,  THAT  IS  ONLY  WHAT  YOU  ARE  CALLED WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE"  HE  ASKED  AGAIN THE  MAN  THOUGHT  FOR  A  MOMENT,  AND  REPLIED  "I  AM  A  PROFESSOR" "THAT  IS  WHAT  YOU  DO,  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE,"  REPLIED  THE  MASTER "WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE" CONFUSED,  THE  MAN  THOUGHT  SOME  MORE FINALLY,  HE  ANSWERED,  "I  AM  A  HUMAN  BEING" "THAT  IS  ONLY  YOUR  SPECIES,  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE",  ASKED  THE  MASTER  AGAIN AFTER  A  MOMENT  OF  THOUGHT,  THE  PROFESSOR  REPLIED  "I  AM  A  CONSCIOUSNESS  INHABITING  AN  ARBITRARY  BODY" "THAT  IS  MERELY  WHAT  YOU  ARE,  NOT  WHO  YOU  ARE WHO  ARE  YOU  WHO  WISHES  TO  STUDY  HERE" THE  MAN  WAS  GETTING  IRRITATED "I  AM,"  HE  STARTED,  BUT  HE  COULD  NOT  THINK  OF  ANYTHING  ELSE  TO  SAY,  SO  HE  TRAILED  OFF AFTER  A  LONG  PAUSE  THE  MASTER  REPLIED,  "THEN  YOU  ARE  WELCOME  TO  COME  STUDY" AN  INSTRUCTION DO  FOUR  UNREASONABLE  THINGS  EACH  DAY

## Visual observations

Bearded figure above a scroll-like frame: A central bearded human figure rises above the rectangular text frame. Spiral ornaments sit on either side near the shoulders, and the bottom of the frame has a shaded, uneven edge with curled sides. This arrangement appears on LP1-06 through LP1-09. Left-facing insect between dialogue and instruction: Below the closing dialogue and its red punctuation cluster is a horizontal insect-like figure. Its head faces left and its striped wing extends right. Beneath it, an enlarged red initial and smaller red heading introduce the instruction in the known reading. Compare the left-facing profile on LP1-16; visual similarity alone does not establish exact source-image reuse.

# LP1-10

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 10; combined archive index: 10.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-10.jpg
Image SHA-256: 12ebfe421c129f2ef78d527c1630e358963da8d8dfdf9620eb977980d7967376
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-10.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-10

## Visual observations

Hooded figures framing the text: Two long hooded human figures flank the central rectangular text panel. Their faces are visible near the top; sweeping curved lines connect the upper decoration, and further loops appear below the panel. The composition has a broadly bilateral arrangement. This observation does not establish exact pixel reflection, identify the figures, or attribute a source artwork.

Red decimal 1 beside the lower passage: A red decimal 1 precedes the lower two-row passage. In the known reading, it introduces the first of the two errors listed under consumption. LP1-11 continues that list with a red 2.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

## Contextual whole-section reading

Section spans: lp1-10, lp1-11, lp1-12, lp1-13

THE LOSS OF DIVINITY THE CIRCUMFERENCE PRACTICES THREE BEHAVIORS WHICH CAUSE THE LOSS OF DIVINITY CONSUMPTION WE CONSUME TOO MUCH BECAUSE WE BELIEVE THE FOLLOWING TWO ERRORS WITHIN THE DECEPTION 1 WE DO NOT HAVE ENOUGH, OR THERE IS NOT ENOUGH 2 WE HAVE WHAT WE HAVE NOW BY LUCK; AND WE WILL NOT BE STRONG ENOUGH LATER TO OBTAIN WHAT WE NEED MOST THINGS ARE NOT WORTH CONSUMING PRESERVATION WE PRESERVE THINGS BECAUSE WE BELIEVE WE ARE WEAK IF WE LOSE THEM WE WILL NOT BE STRONG ENOUGH TO GAIN THEM AGAIN THIS IS THE DECEPTION MOST THINGS ARE NOT WORTH PRESERVING ADHERENCE WE FOLLOW DOGMA SO THAT WE CAN BELONG AND BE RIGHT; OR WE FOLLOW REASON SO WE CAN BELONG AND BE RIGHT THERE IS NOTHING TO BE RIGHT ABOUT; TO BELONG IS DEATH IT IS THE BEHAVIORS OF CONSUMPTION, PRESERVATION AND ADHERENCE THAT HAVE US LOSE OUR PRIMALITY, AND THUS OUR DIVINITY SOME WISDOM AMASS GREAT WEALTH NEVER BECOME ATTACHED TO WHAT YOU OWN BE PREPARED TO DESTROY ALL THAT YOU OWN AN INSTRUCTION PROGRAM YOUR MIND PROGRAM REALITY

# LP1-11

Release: LP1; zero-based release index: 11; combined archive index: 11.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp1-11.jpg
Image SHA-256: 7bd11a2c9f5b512e33c9db170756e3b34cc1e29eb405373eb94957383a61be7d
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp1-11.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-11

## Visual observations

Hooded figures framing the text: Two long hooded human figures flank the central rectangular text panel. Their faces are visible near the top; sweeping curved lines connect the upper decoration, and further loops appear below the panel. The composition has a broadly bilateral arrangement. This observation does not establish exact pixel reflection, identify the figures, or attribute a source artwork.

Red decimal 2 at the opening row: A red decimal 2 precedes the first black runes at the top of the text panel. It continues the numbered list begun on LP1-10; the known reading associates this item with obtaining resources by luck and fearing future inability.

Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp1-12

## Visual observations

Hooded figures framing the text: Two long hooded human figures flank the central rectangular text panel. Their faces are visible near the top; sweeping curved lines connect the upper decoration, and further loops appear below the panel. The composition has a broadly bilateral arrangement. This observation does not establish exact pixel reflection, identify the figures, or attribute a source artwork.

Red heading after the opening continuation: The page begins with two short rows of black runes and a red dotted mark. Below them, a red rune heading introduces the next black-text block. In the known reading, the opening finishes the preservation passage and the red heading reads ADHERENCE.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

ᚳ-ᚠ-ᛈᚪᛚᚢᛠᚾᛚᛄ-ᛄᚳᛚᚹᛠᛞᚢᛞᛇ-ᛠᛉ/

ᚦᛠᛖᛏᚷ-ᚦᚻᚩᛡᚹᚫᛄᛖ-ᛝᛠᛞ-ᚩᚫ-ᚪᛚ-ᛒᛄ/
ᚳᚢᛉᛏᚪᛒᛄᛈ-ᚠᛠ-ᚻᛞᚾᛡᚢᛈᛋᚢᚹ./

Curled borders on both sides: Long curved lines with inward curls frame the left and right sides of the rune column. The border is divided into upper and lower drawings. This motif recurs across LP2-03 through LP2-07; recurrence does not establish an exact pixel match or a shared cipher.

Two text blocks with red opening runes: The text is divided into an upper and a lower block. Each begins with an enlarged red rune beside its first three rows, followed by smaller red runes on the opening row before the text turns black. The two blocks are separated by a broad blank gap.

Curled borders on both sides: Long curved lines with inward curls frame the left and right sides of the rune column. The border is divided into upper and lower drawings. This motif recurs across LP2-03 through LP2-07; recurrence does not establish an exact pixel match or a shared cipher.

Curled borders on both sides: Long curved lines with inward curls frame the left and right sides of the rune column. The border is divided into upper and lower drawings. This motif recurs across LP2-03 through LP2-07; recurrence does not establish an exact pixel match or a shared cipher.

# LP2-07

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 7; combined archive index: 24.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-07.jpg
Image SHA-256: 91a726a7dd59c6caa4d736b9ce72ceba0a2fa827d6b69a2d4057562b9303636c
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-07.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-07

## Visual observations

Curled borders on both sides: Long curved lines with inward curls frame the left and right sides of the rune column. The border is divided into upper and lower drawings. This motif recurs across LP2-03 through LP2-07; recurrence does not establish an exact pixel match or a shared cipher.

Red closing line: Below the black text is a short red line, with compact red punctuation at its ends. It is visually separate from the five much larger black dots lower on the page.

Five large dots below the text: Five separated black dots lie below the red line in a loose arrangement, not a single horizontal row. Small specks beside the upper border curves are a different set of marks and should not be silently included in this count.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

ᛞᛡ-ᛏᛋᛗᛠᛄᛈ-ᛠᛟ-ᛡᚫᚦᚹᚻᛈᛇᚪᚷᛈᚻ/
ᛠ-ᚳᛚᛠᛈ-ᛡᚣᚾᛁ-ᛚᛡᛁᚳ-ᚫᛇᚾ-ᚫᚳᛡᚱᛡᛚ/
ᛞ-ᛒᛟᛝᛡ-ᛉᛗᛝ-ᚳᚻᛟᛠᚾᛈᚳᚦ-ᛁᛇᚦ-ᛇᚢᚩ/
-ᚦᛈᚪ-ᛡᛚᛟᚹᛡᛈ-ᛄᛗ-ᚷᛒᛈᛋᚾᛇ-ᛏᚩᚷᚢᚾᚫ/
ᛖ-ᚾᚣᛁᛖ-ᛞᛝ-ᛞᛝ-ᛚᚢᛚᛉ-ᚪᚾᛝ-ᛇᚪᛄ-ᚻ-ᛞ/
ᚹᛈᚫᚹᚫ-ᛇᛁᛚᛝ-ᚦᚾᚳ.ᛒᛁᛏ-ᛠᚳᚩᛇᛖᛝ-ᚳᚻ/
ᛟᚻᚫᛄ-ᛟᛉ-ᛁᚳᛖᛏᛋᚹᛖᚾᛡᚣᛄᛗ-ᛖᚳᚪ./
ᛞᚩ-ᛟᛏᚦᚫ.ᚳᚹᛄ-ᛉᛠ-ᚷᛠᛗ./
&
$

# LP2-08

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 8; combined archive index: 25.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-08.jpg
Image SHA-256: 6b1026dfdfb447a5a76819883fe576254e8a47fdf1e97ecf1825166833bc6f00
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-08.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-08

## Visual observations

Branching drawing on the left: A slender branching drawing occupies the left margin, with the rune column to its right. The line spreads into multiple tips near its upper and lower ends. Across LP2-08 through LP2-14, the occupied margin alternates left and right; this describes placement, not a verified reflection of the drawing.

Large red opening rune: An enlarged red opening rune extends alongside the first three text rows. Smaller red runes follow it along the opening row, before the text turns black. The branch stands separately in the left margin.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

## Archived transcription

ᛉᛁᛉᛗ-ᚢᛉᛗᚳᚦᛈᚩᛒ-ᛡᚾᛏ-ᛠᛉ/
-ᛈᚱᚣ-ᚩᚳᛠᛗᛝᚷᛉᛚᚢ-ᛝᛁᛏᚩ-/
ᛄᚠᛝ-ᛋᛚᚾᛞ.ᚩᛗ-ᛇᚫ-ᚱᛞᚹᛏᛄᚦ-/
ᚣᚦᛋ-ᚫᚣᛖᛋᛉᛟᛒ-ᛠᚱᛇ-ᛈᛝᚢᛈ-ᚩᚦᛉ-ᚪᚻ/
ᛟᚱᛝᚢᛖᚱ-ᚣᛚᛉᛚ-ᛡᛚᚱ-ᛈᚹᛇᚾ-ᛠᚪᚱᛉᛝ-/
ᚣᛋᚻᚢᛚ-ᛋᚣ-ᚷᚾᚢ-ᛇᚫᚾᚾ-ᚩᚫᛖᛞ-ᚪᚩᛄᛡᚢ/
ᚪᛉ-ᚱᛉᛡᛟᛄ-ᛗᛁᛇᛚᛠᚻᚦᛗᛠᚣ.ᚷᛒᚳᛈ/
ᛉᚳ-ᚾᛟᛟᛋᚷᛗᛈᛖᛏᛚᚾᛄ-ᛄᚳᛝᚩ-ᛁᚹᛚᛠᛒ-/
ᚠᚪᛖ-ᛏᛝ-ᚾᛈᛠᚩᛏᚦ-ᚻᛝᛉᛈᚻᛈᚳᛈᚱᚢ-ᛚ/
ᚠᛖᛟ-ᚷᚪᛒᚠᛁᚫᚠᚢᛟ-ᛗᚠᚣᛝᛄᚳ-ᚻᛏᚠᛚᚫ-ᛖ/
ᚦᛋᛚᚩᚢ-ᚫᚩᚪᛗᛟᚢᚹᛇ.ᛒᚾᛋᛚᛝᛄᛟᚾ-ᛗᛚᛒ-/
ᛟᛏ-ᚾᛞᛒᚩᚾᚦᛡᚻᛟ-ᚱᛈᚾᚠᛈᛞ-ᛋᚩᛁᛠᚣᚾ-ᛇ/

Branching drawing on the left: A slender branching drawing occupies the left margin, with the rune column to its right. The line spreads into multiple tips near its upper and lower ends. Across LP2-08 through LP2-14, the occupied margin alternates left and right; this describes placement, not a verified reflection of the drawing.

# LP2-14

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 14; combined archive index: 31.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-14.jpg
Image SHA-256: 861037ea304b4d3b347cce18d97f25146f6f318cb748e59e6140d9eeaef6abd4
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-14.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-14

## Visual observations

Insect in profile below the text: An insect-like figure lies below the text toward the right. Its curved body is divided into segments, a wing with internal lines rises above it, and long curved appendages extend from the rear. These visible features do not establish a species.

Branching left margin: A narrow, branching drawing runs down the left side, opposite the text and insect. Its upper and lower ends spread into multiple tips. The complete page is needed to compare the two motifs and their placement.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

ᚫᛋᛖ-ᛟᚣᛝᛡ-ᚦᚣᚷᛇᚱ-ᛋᛠᛏ-ᛡᚳᛉ-ᛠᚷ-/

ᛉᚹᛝᚢ-ᛉᛞᛈ.ᛉᛡᛈᛟ-ᚾᛡᚠᛡᚢᛋ-ᛉᚪᛖ/
ᚻᚱᚣᛠᛇ-ᛒᛟ-ᚪᛝᛡ-ᚳᚱᚳᛈᚩᛏ-ᚻᚣᚫᛁᛋᚩᚦᛚ/

# LP2-15

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 15; combined archive index: 32.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-15.jpg
Image SHA-256: 5543cfce96493b86eece3195b3f5ea6e779ff41551676600b0c2479fc18c0ec5
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-15.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-15

## Visual observations

Decimal panel: Sixteen decimal numbers appear in four rows and four columns. 3299 is the only red entry; 708 is the only three-digit entry.

Open-loop drawing: Below the number panel are two open lobes with a crossing, resembling an infinity sign. Visible gaps remain in the drawing. Its intended meaning is not established.

Header: The red header contains nine runes in groups of four and five: F U L M / A EA Y OE A. Latin labels are transliterations, not plaintext.

Printed decimal rows:
3258 3222 3152 3038
3278 3299 3298 2838
3288 3294 3296 2472
4516 1206 708 1820

Black text without the opening panel: Twelve rows of black runes occupy a central column. There is no number panel, crossed loop, red opening, or separate margin illustration on this sheet. Its position after LP2-15 does not by itself tell us whether a cipher key continues or resets.

# LP2-17

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 17; combined archive index: 34.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-17.jpg

Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-17.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-17

## Visual observations

Twelve black rows within blank margins: Twelve rows of black runes occupy a central text block with broad blank margins. No red heading, crossed-loop drawing, or separate illustrated border is visible on this sheet. The community Mobius grouping describes its location in LP2, not a motif repeated on every page.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

ᛚᛟᛁᛇᚣ-ᛝᛡᚾᛏ-ᚱᛁ-ᛋᚪᛖ-ᛇᚢ-ᛝᛞᛄ-ᚠᚱᛠᛗ/
ᛠᚪ-ᚫᛈ-ᛏᚠ-ᛖᛏᚷᚾᚠᛁᚠ-ᚱᚻᚱᛇᛒ.ᚻᛈᛏ-ᛇᚱ/
ᛝᛡᛒᚹᛚᛏ-ᛗᛉᚦ-ᚾᛄᚳᚫ-ᚷᛈ-ᛋᛖᚩ-ᚢᛝᚩ-ᛏ/

ᛠ-ᛇᚦᚩᛉ-ᚾᚱᚾᚫᛁᛉ-ᛁ-ᛝᚣᚫᛡᚫᛗ-ᚹᛖ-ᛇᚷᚻ/

ᚦ-ᚱ-ᛞᛁᚢᚦᚻᛗᛡᚾ-ᛁᚦᚻᛚ.ᛏᚳ-ᚪᚦ-ᚠᚪᚫᚣᚻ/

Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-22

## Visual observations

Red dotted mark at the end of the text: Six rows of black runes end with a narrow red cluster of small square marks. This closing mark is distinct from the black punctuation within the rows. Its color and placement can be recorded without assigning it a decoded meaning.

Horizontal drawing with three crossbars: Below the text is a broad dark horizontal drawing crossed by three thick upright bars. Its right end narrows to a point, and small detached dark marks sit above it. This is a description of the drawing, not an identification of an object or a cipher operation.

Reclining human figure along the bottom edge: A human figure stretches across the bottom of the sheet, with feet at the left and the head at the right. The face is in profile, tilted upward. The image does not establish who the figure represents, whether it is sleeping or dead, or which artwork, if any, supplied a model.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

ᛉ-ᛟᚣ-ᛒᚦᛁᛄᛚᛡᛝᛡ-ᚹᛄᚫ-ᛋᛗᚪᛡᛠᛇᛝᛏ-/

Soft-edged tree-shaped drawing: Below the text is a dark trunk-like form with branching extensions and visibly soft edges. It forms the illustrated endpoint of the community Wing and Tree group, which begins with the wing on LP2-27. The group name is not decrypted text.

Image detail and measurement: Enlarging the drawing changes its display size but does not recover missing detail. Sharpening or thresholding may change the apparent boundaries of branches; such processing should be recorded separately from the preserved original.

Red dotted mark at the end of the text: A narrow red cluster of small square marks follows the final black runes. Compare its visible layout with the closing clusters on LP2-22 and the other illustrated tree page. Similar appearance and placement do not by themselves establish a cipher reset or a shared meaning.

# LP2-36

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 36; combined archive index: 53.

Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-36.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-36

## Visual observations

Cuneiform-like mark above the text: The compact black motif is arranged in two rows above the rune text. It occupies the upper margin, unlike its position below the text on LP2-33. Cuneiform-like is a descriptive community label, not a decoded heading.

Red decimal label 1: A red decimal 1 appears at the left of a new text block below the opening block. It is a printed digit, not a Gematria Primus rune. The numbered sequence continues on LP2-37 and LP2-38; no cipher function is established by its presence.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

## Visual observations

Cuneiform-like mark above the text: The compact black motif is arranged in two rows above the rune text. It occupies the upper margin, unlike its position below the text on LP2-33. Cuneiform-like is a descriptive community label, not a decoded heading.

Red decimal labels 2, 3 and 4: Three red decimal digits mark successive text blocks down the page: 2 at the opening block, 3 at the next, and 4 near the bottom. They continue the 1 on LP2-36 and precede the 5 on LP2-38. These are printed labels, not rune indices inferred from the text.

# LP2-38

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 38; combined archive index: 55.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-38.jpg
Image SHA-256: aec1898f599f57265d6422f3082a481db94a27f62230affbadee595d05077f8c
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-38.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-38

## Visual observations

Cuneiform-like mark above the text: The compact black motif is arranged in two rows above the rune text. It occupies the upper margin, unlike its position below the text on LP2-33. Cuneiform-like is a descriptive community label, not a decoded heading.

Red decimal label 5: A red decimal 5 begins a text block below the opening block. It follows the labels 1 on LP2-36 and 2, 3 and 4 on LP2-37. The opening block on this page has no new decimal label; a page boundary and a numbered-block boundary are therefore different visible features.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

## Archived transcription

ᚢᚫᚳᛇᚳᚣ-ᛡᚫᛏᛖᚳᚠ-ᛋᚻ-ᛋᚱᚢᚦ-ᛁᛋᛝᛗᛞ/

## Visual observations

Cuneiform-like mark above the text: The compact black motif is arranged in two rows above the rune text. It occupies the upper margin, unlike its position below the text on LP2-33. Cuneiform-like is a descriptive community label, not a decoded heading.

Three separated black dots: Three large black dots lie horizontally in the gap between the upper text block and the lower block. They are separate from the smaller punctuation marks within the rune text. Compare the three-dot row on LP2-33.

Enlarged red rune in the lower block: A large red rune begins the lower text block and extends alongside its first three rows. Smaller red runes follow it at the start of the first row. This color and scale change is visible, but does not by itself specify a decryption rule.

# LP2-40

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 40; combined archive index: 57.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-40.jpg
Image SHA-256: 3f5af995b39f94f268d4aa94825a10f2429f4a3affa1921a7f627e6d1bfcfb69
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-40.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-40

## Visual observations

Curled and branching side borders: Long black stems frame both sides of the text, combining large curls with smaller curled branches and root-like ends. A hanging cluster of thin branches occupies the middle of each border. The resemblance between the margins is visible; an exact reflection or reuse of the same source image has not been established by this observation.

Left border: solid marks and pale rings: The left cluster contains three solid black marks and two pale outlined rings. The outlines are much fainter than the solid marks, so a dark-pixel threshold can omit them. Inspect the original colors before treating all five positions as equivalent.

Right border: five solid marks: The right cluster contains five solid black marks. Compare its fill with the left cluster on this same page. The difference is visible; a binary encoding or a numerical meaning has not been established.

Red opening beside three rows: An enlarged red opening rune extends alongside the first three text rows. Smaller red runes and red punctuation occupy the beginning of the first row before the text turns black. Lower rows include pairs of short upright marks; their appearance is separate from any role assigned in a transcription.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-53

## Visual observations

Winged figure beneath the text: A dark outlined figure with a narrow body and outspread wings sits below the text. The wings contain internal lines and shaded areas. Compare LP2-55 for a similar subject; this observation does not establish the same source drawing or a species.

Curled side borders: Tall curled and branching forms flank the text. Their lower ends spread into root-like tips beside the winged figure. Similar placement on the two sides is visible, but exact reflection or pixel equality has not been established.

Black-to-red text transition: The upper text is black. A red rune appears at the right end of a row otherwise printed in black, and the following lower rows are red. A color-based extraction would need to record that change within the row rather than assume it coincides with a row boundary.

Left border: solid marks and pale rings: The left cluster contains three solid black marks and two pale outlined rings. The outlines are much fainter than the solid marks, so a dark-pixel threshold can omit them. Inspect the original colors before treating all five positions as equivalent.

Right border: five solid marks: The right cluster contains five solid black marks. Compare its fill with the left cluster on this same page. The difference is visible; a binary encoding or a numerical meaning has not been established.

## Visual observations

Curled and branching side borders: Long black stems frame both sides of the text, combining large curls with smaller curled branches and root-like ends. A hanging cluster of thin branches occupies the middle of each border. The resemblance between the margins is visible; an exact reflection or reuse of the same source image has not been established by this observation.

Left border: solid marks and pale rings: The left cluster contains three solid black marks and two pale outlined rings. The outlines are much fainter than the solid marks, so a dark-pixel threshold can omit them. Inspect the original colors before treating all five positions as equivalent.

Right border: five solid marks: The right cluster contains five solid black marks. Compare its fill with the left cluster on this same page. The difference is visible; a binary encoding or a numerical meaning has not been established.

Red opening beside three rows: An enlarged red opening rune extends alongside the first three text rows. Smaller red runes follow on the first row, ending at a compact red punctuation cluster before black text continues. The pale tree and winged figure associated with this two-page community group appear on LP2-55, not on this page.

# LP2-55

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 55; combined archive index: 72.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: unsolved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-55.jpg
Image SHA-256: a80191592add93a86ed3868f9e4e6ba3944ec20c9ffccc7d3e221b461344beba
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-55.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-55

## Visual observations

Pale tree above a winged figure: A pale gray, tree-shaped outline lies between the short text block and a dark winged figure at the bottom. The tree and insect-like figure are separate visible elements. The tree has branching contours and a trunk-like base; its intended meaning and source are not established.

Winged figure and curled borders: The lower figure has outspread wings with dark internal detail. Curled, branching borders run down the left and right margins. Compare the layout with LP2-53, keeping the added tree and the different amount of text in view.

Red dotted mark at the end of the text: A narrow red cluster of small square marks follows the final black runes. Compare its visible layout with the closing clusters on LP2-22 and the other illustrated tree page. Similar appearance and placement do not by themselves establish a cipher reset or a shared meaning.

# LP2-56

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 56; combined archive index: 73.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-56.jpg
Image SHA-256: a4c1c9ae1246c3197fc1d7bd0155cbc97f60d4bba84a104d45f180feab1814dc
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-56.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-56

## Visual observations

Five large black dots below the text: Five filled black dots form a loose arrangement below the final two runic rows. They are much larger than the small red punctuation clusters within the text. This is another five-dot arrangement to compare with LP2-07 and LP2-23; the count alone does not identify a symbol, reading order or decoding instruction.

Hexadecimal block between runic passages: Five rows of Latin hexadecimal characters sit between an upper runic passage and two lower runic rows. The characters are printed directly on the page. The target guide joins those rows into one 128-character string while retaining their original display breaks.

Red opening and small red closing marks: An enlarged red initial stands beside the upper passage, with smaller red runes on its first row. Small red punctuation clusters close the upper and lower runic passages. The large black dots farther below are a separate visual feature.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

# LP2-57

Release: LP2; zero-based release index: 57; combined archive index: 74.
Status in source snapshot dated 2026-10-05: solved.

Original image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/images/lp2-57.jpg
Image SHA-256: 1dabc100ddbf1fc49715219636984eb6ad96a2bd8035e196c12e66db77a1077b
Structured record: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/pages/lp2-57.json
Human reader: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/reader/lp2-57

## Visual observations

Stippled insect-like figure: Below the final parable is a figure formed from many small black marks. A dense central body extends downward, with scattered marks spreading into wing-like areas on both sides. This rendering differs from the outlined and shaded winged figures on LP2-53 and LP2-55.

Red opening and punctuation: The text begins with an enlarged red rune beside the first three rows and smaller red runes on the opening row. Red punctuation clusters also appear in the text. Their visual color should be kept separate from the rune-only prime sums calculated from the known reading.

Visual observation record (selected observations, original-image hashes and review date): https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/evidence/editorial-page-notes.json

Liberpedia / Reference
Gematria Primus

Alphabet reference · 29 symbols

The alphabet assigns a Latin label and a prime number to each of 29 runes. A zero-based index is useful for describing the order of the alphabet, but it is a different quantity from the prime value.

For example, ᚠ has index 0, Latin label F, and prime value 2. Labels such as TH and NG represent a single rune, not two symbols.

Rune	Latin label	Index (0–28)	Prime value	Aliases
ᚠ	F	0	2	F
ᚢ	U	1	3	U
ᚦ	TH	2	5	TH
ᚩ	O	3	7	O
ᚱ	R	4	11	R
ᚳ	C	5	13	C, K
ᚷ	G	6	17	G
ᚹ	W	7	19	W
ᚻ	H	8	23	H
ᚾ	N	9	29	N
ᛁ	I	10	31	I
ᛄ	J	11	37	J
ᛇ	EO	12	41	EO
ᛈ	P	13	43	P
ᛉ	X	14	47	X
ᛋ	S	15	53	S, Z
ᛏ	T	16	59	T
ᛒ	B	17	61	B
ᛖ	E	18	67	E
ᛗ	M	19	71	M
ᛚ	L	20	73	L
ᛝ	NG	21	79	NG, ING
ᛟ	OE	22	83	OE
ᛞ	D	23	89	D
ᚪ	A	24	97	A
ᚫ	AE	25	101	AE
ᚣ	Y	26	103	Y
ᛡ	IA	27	107	IA, IO
ᛠ	EA	28	109	EA
Reading the labels

Latin labels are transcription conventions. They do not, by themselves, decrypt the text. U/V and C/K may be represented differently in a contextual English reading. Keep the rune sequence available when comparing such readings.

Source: archived Gematria Primus chart · community reference.

Liberpedia / Reference
Transcription guide

Numbering, symbols, and editorial conventions

Page identifiers

LP1 contains pages 00–16; LP2 contains pages 00–57. These numbers identify the order in the public archive. They are not page numbers printed on every manuscript image. Use the release prefix when citing a page.

Three different representations
Original image: the preserved JPEG, including artwork, color, placement, and punctuation.
Archived transcription: a community-created symbolic representation of that image.
Known reading: a documented decoded or readable interpretation, shown separately when available.

Transcriptions cannot preserve every visual distinction. A delimiter in the text is not automatically proof of a particular printed mark or grammatical meaning.

Archive delimiter notation
Notation	Archive convention
-	Word separator
,	Three-dot symbol
.	Clause separator
&	Paragraph separator
$	Segment separator
§	Chapter separator
/	Line boundary
%	Page boundary

These names describe the transcription convention, not an independently established cipher function.

Corrections and measurements

The page record retains the archived text. Where a documented visual review identifies a correction, the record lists it explicitly and offers a separate reviewed-text view. Character offsets are zero-based positions in the archived Unicode text.

Rune counts and prime-value sums are calculated from the archived rune sequence. Decimal digits and punctuation do not contribute to these sums. Such totals describe the transcription; they are not proposed cipher keys.

Image coordinates

Recorded regions use the original JPEG pixels: x and y begin at the upper-left corner. Each rectangle is written as x, y, width, height. Cropped thumbnails are browsing aids; the full original and its checksum remain available.

Liberpedia · Sources & provenance · Source snapshot: 5 October 2026

Method, key, and counting conventions

p = 28 − c. Here c and p are zero-based rune indices in the 29-symbol alphabet.

Welcome, Pilgrim	LP1–03 · LP1–04	vigenere
Method, key, and counting conventions

p = (c − key[j mod key length]) mod 29. Here c and p are zero-based rune indices in the 29-symbol alphabet.

Key indices: 23, 10, 1, 10, 9, 10, 16, 26
Literal key labels: DIUINITY.

The sequence starts at position 0. Continue the sequence across the listed pages in order. Non-rune characters do not advance the sequence.

Copy the runes at these zero-based positions without advancing the sequence: 48, 74, 84, 132, 159, 160, 250, 421, 443, 465, 514. Positions count runes across the listed section, excluding punctuation and decimal digits.

These positions were aligned to known readings. They do not establish a rule to skip every F or apply the same interruptions to unsolved pages.

The deep-web page reference	LP2–56	prime-minus-one
Method, key, and counting conventions

p = (c − (prime[j] − 1)) mod 29. Here c and p are zero-based rune indices in the 29-symbol alphabet.

The sequence starts at position 0. Prime position 0 is 2; subsequent primes are 3, 5, 7, and so on. The sequence resets at the page boundary. Non-rune characters do not advance the sequence.

Copy the runes at these zero-based positions without advancing the sequence: 56. Positions count runes across the listed section, excluding punctuation and decimal digits.

These positions were aligned to known readings. They do not establish a rule to skip every F or apply the same interruptions to unsolved pages.

Archived walkthrough · Recorded parameters and provenance


Parable	LP2–57	direct
Method, key, and counting conventions

p = c. Here c and p are zero-based rune indices in the 29-symbol alphabet.

Archived walkthrough · Recorded parameters and provenance

Before comparing spellings

Latin labels can use U for V and C for K, while a single rune may represent several Latin letters. These conventions can make a literal reading look unusual. Use the alphabet reference and preserve the underlying rune sequence.

The LP1-10 I/E correction is a documented transcription issue. It is shown beside the archived text instead of being silently replaced.

Evidence distinctions
Record	What it establishes
Original-format image	The preserved appearance and bytes of a public archive artifact.
Community transcription	A readable representation to inspect against the image; transcription mistakes remain possible.
Recorded visual observation	A specific inspection or measurement, limited to its stated region.
Known reading	An established reading from the archived solution record, distinct from raw rune labels.

Liberpedia / Reference
Spelling, rune choices, and prime sums

Exact arithmetic · Source spellings · What the numerical patterns establish

The exact rune sequence determines the number. A polished English rendering can conceal numerical structure by changing how several letters are represented. Some unusual spellings have numerical consequences; others are aliases, reorderings, or transcription errors.

The strongest example here is LP2-57: each of its three body sentences has a prime sum that reverses to another prime. We can verify that property. Whether each individual spelling was chosen specifically to produce it is a separate question.

1. Define the sum before interpreting it

For rune sequence r₁, …, rₙ, use S = GP(r₁) + … + GP(rₙ), where GP is the rune’s prime value in Gematria Primus. Count each rune once. These calculations exclude punctuation, spaces, line markers, and decimal digits.

Keep three choices explicit: which text (ciphertext or known decoded text), which boundary (word, sentence, or page), and which encoding (one multi-letter rune or several individual runes). Changing a choice changes the question being answered.

All examples below use the known decoded rune sequence. LP2-57 and LP1-16 are directly readable; WIDSOM on LP1-04 is taken from its documented keyed reading. The ordinary page sidebar’s prime sum instead describes the archived rune sequence.

2. LP2-57: sentence sums and emirps

An emirp is a prime whose decimal reversal is a different prime. The three body sentences, using the archive’s clause boundaries, have this property:

Text segment	Rune sum	Decimal reversal	Result
PARABLE — heading	449	944	449 is prime; 944 is composite
Like the instar tunneling to the surface.	1259	9521	Both prime; emirp
We must shed our own circumferences.	1031	1301	Both prime; emirp
Find the divinity within and emerge.	1229	9221	Both prime; emirp

The complete heading-plus-body total is 3968 = 2⁷ × 31, which is composite. “All numbers are prime” is therefore too broad. The boundary is part of the observation: the three body sentence sums are emirps; the whole-page sum is not prime.

Inspect every rune value in these four sums
PARABLE

ᛈᚪᚱᚪᛒᛚᛖ

43 + 97 + 11 + 97 + 61 + 73 + 67 = 449

LICE-THE-INSTAR-TUNNELNG-TO-THE-SURFACE

ᛚᛁᚳᛖᚦᛖᛁᚾᛋᛏᚪᚱᛏᚢᚾᚾᛖᛚᛝᛏᚩᚦᛖᛋᚢᚱᚠᚪᚳᛖ

73 + 31 + 13 + 67 + 5 + 67 + 31 + 29 + 53 + 59 + 97 + 11 + 59 + 3 + 29 + 29 + 67 + 73 + 79 + 59 + 7 + 5 + 67 + 53 + 3 + 11 + 2 + 97 + 13 + 67 = 1259

WE-MUST-SHED-OUR-OWN-CIRCUMFERENCES

ᚹᛖᛗᚢᛋᛏᛋᚻᛖᛞᚩᚢᚱᚩᚹᚾᚳᛁᚱᚳᚢᛗᚠᛖᚱᛖᚾᚳᛖᛋ

19 + 67 + 71 + 3 + 53 + 59 + 53 + 23 + 67 + 89 + 7 + 3 + 11 + 7 + 19 + 29 + 13 + 31 + 11 + 13 + 3 + 71 + 2 + 67 + 11 + 67 + 29 + 13 + 67 + 53 = 1031

FIND-THE-DIUINITY-WITHIN-AND-EMERGE

ᚠᛁᚾᛞᚦᛖᛞᛁᚢᛁᚾᛁᛏᚣᚹᛁᚦᛁᚾᚪᚾᛞᛖᛗᛖᚱᚷᛖ

2 + 31 + 29 + 89 + 5 + 67 + 89 + 31 + 3 + 31 + 29 + 31 + 59 + 103 + 19 + 31 + 5 + 31 + 29 + 97 + 29 + 89 + 67 + 71 + 67 + 11 + 17 + 67 = 1229

Why expanding the English spelling changes the result

The “NG” rune can stand for NG or ING. In the archived direct reading, TUNNELNG corresponds to contextual English “tunneling.” Adding an I rune when re-encoding that English word adds 31. Keeping everything else fixed changes the first sentence from 1259 to 1290 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 43. The emirp property disappears.

This gives a concrete numerical reason to preserve the original encoding. It does not make the NG/ING alias a spelling mistake: one rune legitimately represents several Latin letters. Inspect the original sequence.

3. Work through the spellings individually

CWESTIAN
ᚳᚹᛖᛋᛏᛡᚾ	13 + 19 + 67 + 53 + 59 + 107 + 29	347

	LP1-16

ᚹᛁᛞᛋᚩᛗ	19 + 31 + 89 + 53 + 7 + 71	270

	LP1-04

ᛒᛖᛚᛁᛖᚢᛖ	61 + 67 + 73 + 31 + 67 + 3 + 67	369

	LP1-10

ᚠᚢᚾᚳᛏᛡᚾ	2 + 3 + 29 + 13 + 59 + 107 + 29	242

ᛁᛚᛚᚢᛋᛡᚾᛋ	31 + 73 + 73 + 3 + 53 + 107 + 29 + 53	422

	LP1-03

ᛋᚢᚠᚠᛖᚱᛝ	53 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 67 + 11 + 79	217

Composite
	LP1-03
CWESTIAN / KWESTION: the exact encoding matters

The seven labels are C · W · E · S · T · IA · N. C/K and IA/IO are alternative Latin labels for the same runes, so CWESTIAN and KWESTION can describe the same rune sequence. Its sum is 13 + 19 + 67 + 53 + 59 + 107 + 29 = 347, a prime.

For an explicit comparison, keep C W E S T and N fixed, but replace the single IA/IO rune (107) with separate I and O runes (31 + 7). The total becomes 347 − 107 + 31 + 7 = 278 = 2 × 139. This alternate rune encoding is composite. It is a counterfactual comparison, not text found on the page.

The conventional spelling QUESTION cannot be assigned a unique GP sum without an additional spelling rule: the chart has no separate Q rune. Quietly converting Q into some preferred sequence would build an assumption into the result. We can establish the printed encoding’s prime sum without claiming that this proves why the author selected it.

WIDSOM / WISDOM: reordering cannot tune an additive sum

Both use the same six rune values and sum to 270 = 2 × 3³ × 5. Swapping D and S changes their order, not their sum. The same holds for every larger word or sentence total containing that swap while keeping its boundary fixed.

Formally, for any permutation π, Σ GP(rᵢ) = Σ GP(rπ(i)). An order-sensitive cipher can distinguish the spellings; an additive prime sum cannot. WIDSOM is preserved in the known keyed reading of LP1-04, while WISDOM appears in LP1-05. Neither word total is prime.

If a calculation adds a delimiter value of 1, then 270 + 1 = 271, which is prime. That is a different counting convention, and it gives the same result for both word orders. The rune-only chart does not supply this extra 1. A punctuation-inclusive claim must state and justify its delimiter rule rather than quietly add it after seeing the total.

BELIEUE / BELEIUE: a transcription correction, not prime fitting

The native-image correction on LP1-10 restores BELIEUE from the archived I/E reversal. Both orders sum to 369 = 3² × 41. The correction matters for fidelity and sequence-sensitive work, but it cannot make an unchanged additive word or sentence sum prime. The U/V rendering in contextual BELIEVE does not add another rune.

FUNCTIAN, ILLUSIANS, SUFFERNG: aliases can look like omissions

IA/IO and NG/ING account for these literal forms. Their rune sums are 242, 422, and 217, all composite. Replacing IA/IO with separate I and O decreases the first two sums by 69, producing 173 and 353, both prime. Adding I before NG in SUFFERNG produces 248, composite.

These contrasting examples matter: the observed spelling does not universally maximize word-level primality. A claim about “fitting the primes” must name the intended boundary and evaluate the complete specified set, including examples that do not fit.

4. What can we say about purpose?

Established numerical property: the three LP2-57 body sentences have emirp sums under the stated rune-only convention. CWESTIAN’s recorded rune sequence has a prime word sum. The calculations are reproducible.

Numerical consequence: some plausible alternative encodings change these properties. Pure reorderings and alias relabelings leave additive sums unchanged. Transcription mistakes must be corrected from source evidence, not selected to improve a number.

Proposed purpose: exact wording and rune choices may have been constrained to produce particular totals, possibly as structural markers or consistency checks. These are interpretations of the pattern, not an authenticated explanation of intent. The known text’s statements about sacred primes provide relevant context, but do not specify a universal spelling-selection rule.

A useful test fixes the target unit, segmentation, punctuation values, and allowed alternatives before counting. Count all matches and non-matches. Searching many boundaries, aliases, reversals, and offsets creates many opportunities to find a prime; a selected hit alone does not quantify how surprising it is. No calibrated probability of authorial intent is claimed here.

## Original image, mirror, and authentication

Subject: Checking a source

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=image-evidence

Image checksums identify preserved bytes. Agreement between mirrors can reflect a shared ancestor and does not establish who created or signed the complete image.

Search terms: original authentic authenticity signature signed sha256 checksum hash provenance evidence mirror

- Sources and evidence distinctions: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/sources
- Image checksum manifest: https://jelliottdev.github.io/data/manifest.json

Evidence basis: Archive provenance and recorded image hashes.

## Which images contain stored OutGuess messages?

Subject: Checking a source

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=hidden-messages

Find the payload inventory, extract preserved bytes, and follow the opening, title-page, and illustrated-cover chains.

Search terms: outguess steganography hidden stored embedded payload message jpeg title cover

- Payload inventory: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/embedded-payloads
- Extract with OutGuess: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/outguess
- 2014 opening image: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/opening-2014
- Cover payload chain: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/cover-chain
- Illustrated-cover RSA: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/cover-rsa

Evidence basis: The inventory and extraction guide retain image and payload checksums and separate embedded bytes from later transformations.

## A matching file hash is not a signature

Subject: Checking a source

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=hashes-signatures

Check that a download matches the preserved bytes, then examine what a PGP signature can establish about a message.

Search terms: sha256 hash checksum pgp gpg signature verify authentic provenance download

- File checksums: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/checksums
- PGP signatures: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/pgp-signatures
- LP2-56 hash target: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/lp2-56-target

Evidence basis: Integrity checks, message-signature verification, and the unsolved hash target are different operations.

## Solid dots and pale rings on LP2-53

Subject: Image details

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=border-rings

The left border contains three solid marks and two pale ring outlines; the right has five solid marks. Compare the enlarged original-image views before counting all ten shapes as equivalent.

Search terms: hollow outlined circles rings dots border 53

- Compare the two borders: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/dots?section=border-dots
- LP2-53 visual notes: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/page/lp2-53?section=details

Evidence basis: Selected observations of the preserved JPEG. Shape and count do not establish a cipher function.

## Why do the branches change sides?

Subject: Image details

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=alternating-branches

Across LP2-08–14, the branch drawing alternates between the left and right margins. The comparison lists each page and separates a change of position from an actual reflected image.

Search terms: alternating branches margins left right mirror reflection 08 09 10 11 12 13 14

- Compare the alternating margins: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/branches?section=alternating-margins
- LP2-08 visual notes: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/page/lp2-08?section=details
- LP2-09 visual notes: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/page/lp2-09?section=details

Evidence basis: Original-image observations; reversal as a decoding instruction remains a hypothesis.

## The red numbers 1–5 beside the text

Subject: Image details

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=red-number-labels

The labels continue across three pages: 1 on LP2-36, 2–4 on LP2-37, and 5 on LP2-38. A numbered block is not the same boundary as a page break.

Search terms: red numbers labels numbered blocks cuneiform cuniform 1 2 3 4 5

- Follow the numbers across pages: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/cuneiform?section=number-labels
- LP2-37 visual notes: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/page/lp2-37?section=details

Evidence basis: Visible decimal labels in the original images; their role in a cipher is not established.

## How the second koan refers to its own argument

Subject: Ideas and referenced works

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=koan-self-reference

The student thinks a denial of the master’s claim. The master then treats that thought as an example of the inner voice being discussed. A diagram follows the steps and explains the limits of that interpretation.

Search terms: self reference self-reference self referential koan paradox thought mind reading inner voice

- Follow the argument diagram: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/koans?section=self-reference
- Read the second koan: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/reading-second-koan

Evidence basis: Interpretation of the known reading, not evidence of a demonstrated mind-reading ability.

## Generate all 58 shift-and-reversal candidates

Subject: Decoding and analysis

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=bounded-shifts

Run a small script that enumerates 29 shifts in each of two rune orders. The output records the input hash and every candidate; producing that list does not test whether any candidate is meaningful.

Search terms: caesar shift reverse reversal enumerate candidates 58 brute force script

- Command, output, and limits: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/reproducibility?section=generate-candidates
- Download the script: https://jelliottdev.github.io/scripts/enumerate_shifts.py

Evidence basis: A reproducible candidate-generation exercise, not a completed experiment or a finding about an unsolved page.

## Which number grid is this?

Subject: Decoding and analysis

Topic: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/topics?topic=number-grids

Compare the rune-and-number square on LP1-05, the decimal square on LP1-16, embedded ASCII grids, the LP2-15 panel, and the alphanumeric arrays on LP2-49–51.

Search terms: magic square 1033 3301 mixed grid rune words number panel alphanumeric letter number grid 256 entries

- Compare the grid arrangements: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/magic-squares?section=compare
- Work through the rune-value substitution: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/magic-squares?section=rune-cells
- LP2-15 printed panel: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/lp2-15-panel
- LP2-49–51 letters and numbers: counts, repeats, and downloads: https://jelliottdev.github.io/#/wiki/alphanumeric-grids

Evidence basis: Original page records, preserved embedded messages, and reproducible arithmetic; a matching sum does not establish a cipher key.


---

Start solving: a practical introduction

Find the right pages, reproduce known results, and turn an idea into a test someone else can repeat.

Liber Primus combines visible artwork, rune text, numbers, and hidden file content. Learn how these layers differ before treating them as one cipher. A title image can have no runic paragraph and still carry a signed OutGuess message.

1. Know the collection
The first release contains 17 images, including two title pages. The second release contains 58. In the archived source snapshot, LP1 has known readings and LP2 has readings for 56 and 57; LP2 pages 00–55 remain unsolved. This is dated documented knowledge, not live proof that nobody has solved anything else.
Use IDs such as LP2-31. “Page 31” without a release or archive name is ambiguous. The numbering cross-reference maps release IDs to archive filenames.

The illustrated cover with compasses comes from an earlier puzzle stage and has its own entry. It is different from LP1-00, the plain title page, and does not change the release numbering.

[Image: The warning page used for the first reading exercise]
LP1-01: start here. Its known Atbash reading makes a short, checkable first exercise.
[Image: LP2-31, an unsolved page used in the statistics guide]
LP2-31: a later investigation. Its recorded measurements describe the text; they do not supply a decryption.

2. Reproduce one short reading
Open the warning in the reader. Compare the original image with its runes, then follow the complete warning reading and its Atbash explanation. Use the 29-symbol alphabet, not English A–Z. Count a multi-letter rune as one symbol.

python scripts/verify_bundle.py REFERENCE-DATA-CONTENTS.json
python scripts/reproduce_reading.py warning
python scripts/reproduce_reading.py --check-all
Download and extract the reference-data ZIP, then run these commands from the extracted folder with Python 3. Keep the folders together: the script reads the included text and parameter files. After the file check, the warning command prints its literal reading; --check-all checks all 17 known runic-page outputs. All three commands run locally with the Python standard library and make no AI requests. A full repository checkout also works.

The first command checks the extracted files against the bundle’s own manifest and should report 0 problems. It does not authenticate the manifest. If it reports missing or changed files, follow the setup check before interpreting a decoding result.

What success looks like

The warning output begins A-WARNNG.BELIEUE-NOTHNG-FROM-. Those spellings are expected literal rune labels, not evidence that the script failed. The complete control check prints:

PASS: 17 literal page readings match the published controls exactly.

This confirms that the supplied recipes reproduce the stored known outputs. It does not independently authenticate the source files or validate a proposed solution to an unsolved page. Use the download catalogue for file hashes and the transliteration guide for the difference between literal labels and contextual English.

Working from a phone? You can do the first arithmetic check without installing anything. In the worked warning example, the first rune has index 4. Subtracting it from 28 gives 24, the label A. The next input index is 21, giving 7, or W. Follow the table against the original image, then read the complete passage. Save the script run for when you have a Python environment.

Optional second check: one row of the number grid
Open LP1-05 and find the five-by-five grid below the text. Its first row mixes four printed numbers with one rune word. In the known reading that word is labeled SHADOWS.
Leave the printed entries 272, 138, 131 and 151 unchanged.
Use the worked rune-cell table to check the word’s seven rune values. Their sum is 341.
Add the row: 272 + 138 + 341 + 131 + 151 = 1033.
This verifies one row, not the whole square. The full explanation shows all five rows, five columns and two main diagonals. If you have Python, python scripts/check_number_examples.py reproduces those checks from the included page and alphabet records.
The important distinction is the input: the printed decimal numbers stay as numbers, while rune words are replaced by additive prime values. Do not apply a prime-index lookup to every entry or replace the words with ordinary English spelling. Those would be different procedures.
New to the terminal? Running the reproduction scripts walks through setup, expected results, trace columns, and common errors.
3. Learn the other layers
Rune indices and prime values: cipher arithmetic versus prime sums.
Vigenère: keys, direction, and continuity across pages.
The cover payload chain: OutGuess, hexadecimal, XOR, signatures, and transposition.
Spelling and prime sums: a reproducible numerical property versus an explanation of a spelling’s purpose.

For the ideas behind the decoded passages, follow the philosophy reading route, then compare the William Blake parallel. These guides distinguish the manuscript words, interpretation, and possible outside sources.

4. Make an idea testable
Choose a page, a region, a transformation, and a success criterion. “Try primes” is too broad. “Subtract consecutive prime-minus-one values modulo 29 from LP2-31, starting at the first rune, advancing the prime sequence only for runes, continuing across punctuation without resetting, and skipping no runes” specifies one test. It does not establish that this is the correct method.
Check Have we tried it? for the technique and scope. The registry is awaiting reviewed records; an empty result means no published match here, not that an idea is new. Follow the reproducibility guide.

Choose one first investigation

You do not need to learn every technique at once. Choose a route that produces a small result someone else can inspect.

	If you want to…	Start with	Keep as your result

	Read and interpret	Compare the warning and later instructions	Exact passages, their locations, and your interpretation stated separately

	Inspect artwork	Compare the insect drawings	Page IDs, visible similarities and differences, and any named comparison source

	Check arithmetic	Reproduce LP1-05’s mixed-grid conversion	The original cells, rune-value substitutions, and all twelve line sums

	Measure a text	Reproduce LP2-31’s IoC	The input hash, rune counts, exact fraction, and a statement of what it cannot establish

	Study a decoding	Trace the Welcome’s repeating key	A few input/output steps, the key position, and the treatment of recorded exceptions


Before expanding a numerical search, check what your operation preserves. For example, whole-stream IoC cannot choose between rearrangements of the same symbols. For literary or visual work, a well-supported comparison is useful even when it supplies no cipher key.

A first observation using only your phone

Open LP2-49 in the reader. Beneath the three runic rows, find the third row of the letter-and-number grid. Count grid rows from one and columns from left to right. This row reads:

21 3M 0F 0X 1g 2H 0x 1R

[Image: Third grid row of LP2-49, including uppercase 0X in column four and lowercase 0x in column seven.]
Detail from the original JPEG, region [600, 1560, 1200, 160]. Download the complete original.

Compare column 4, 0X, with column 7, 0x. The initial character is zero in the archived transcription; the second character differs in case.
Write the observation with its location: “LP2-49, grid row 3: column 4 is transcribed as 0X; column 7 as 0x.”
Keep a proposed explanation separate. This difference does not yet tell you whether the entries encode letters, coordinates, or numbers.

You have now made a small claim another reader can check. The grid transcription guide explains ambiguous characters and leading zeroes; its coordinate exports let you check the same positions in structured data. If you disagree with a glyph, preserve the original transcription and document the proposed correction with the image location.

Find the page behind a quotation

Suppose you remember the phrase “circumference practices” and want to cite it. A complete reading can cover several sheets, so finding the section is only the first step.


Search for "circumference practices", including the quotation marks. LP1-10 is the literal-reading match. Other sheets can appear because their records include the same complete section text.

Open LP1-10’s known reading. The word crosses its first two literal lines: CIRCU/ then MFERENCE. Compare the page’s original image when checking the underlying runes.

Keep the location with your note: “LP1-10, literal reading, lines 1–2; word joined across the line break.” A statement about what the circumference means is your interpretation and needs its own explanation.


With Python, repeat the lookup using python scripts/reading_concordance.py "circumference practices" --literal. Add --json to retain the exact excerpt, character offsets, and page-record checksum. The concordance guide explains those fields and why character positions are not rune indices. This exercise works with a known reading; it does not search for English words inside unsolved ciphertext.

Ready to contribute
You should be able to identify an exact image, distinguish raw from corrected transcription, reproduce a known reading, and explain what would count against your hypothesis. You do not need to understand every cipher before inspecting a well-defined detail.
For a worked descriptive analysis, use the index-of-coincidence baseline: exact rune counts, downloadable results, reproduction commands and the limits of frequency evidence.
Sources and verification
Pinned historical walkthrough. Recipes reproduce published controls; they are not new solutions. Local computational verification: 19 October 2026.
